GHA.note: Data centres are discussed in general; no facility for hire is named.
Nothing on rural programmes or rural-urban use.
The NCA consultation is named but not stated to be run online.

facts.fact: The IMANI Africa piece says Ghana has two exchange points in service, GIXA with 23 members including all major mobile operators and Google, and AccraIX with 21 members including MTN, Telecel, Meta and Fastly.

GHA.note: Says the grid has frequent interruptions but gives no count.
Mentions only the March 2024 subsea cable cuts; no routes are named.
No share of people using the internet is given.
Only says 1 GB costs nearly a day's minimum wage, with no price or income share.
No nationally owned data centre for hire is stated.

facts.fact: The IMANI think-tank writer criticises the government's mandated increase in data bundle volumes as treating the symptom and says the draft Electronic Communications Bill 2025 lacks a mandatory open peering obligation.
IMANI Africa's Centre for Science, Technology and Innovation Policy published this analysis of Ghana's internet exchange and peering policy.
facts.system: IMANI Centre for Science, Technology and Innovation Policy

facts.fact: The National Communications Authority had an ongoing public consultation on the Electronic Communications Bill, 2025, dated 16 October 2025 in the article's references.

GHA.note: Nothing on startup law or funds.
